title: Challenge the golden-brass primary
question: FISHEYE’s primary CTA currently uses Golden Brass (#a67c42). On parchment it can read as beige. Pick a replacement primary/accent for buttons — or keep the current brass. All options keep parchment grounds, ink type, and One Accent Rule unless noted.

options.label: Keep Golden Brass
options.thesis: Leave #a67c42 as the sole action color — rarity over novelty.
options.viewport: Primary buttons stay soft golden brass on parchment and dark bands.
options.case: Safest continuity with The Parchment Atelier; does not address the beige reading.
options.risk: Buttons keep reading warm-beige rather than metallic action.

options.label: Antique Bronze
options.thesis: Same metal metaphor, darker and denser so CTAs stop reading as washed beige.
options.viewport: Primary fill #5c4528 with parchment or near-white label text for contrast.
options.case: Evolves brass without leaving the atelier metal story — most coherent refinement.
options.risk: Still warm-brown family; if you dislike all brown-golds, this may still feel close.

options.label: Ink Action
options.thesis: Architectural minimal: primary CTAs go pure ink; color rarity moves to link underlines only or drops.
options.viewport: Black primary buttons with parchment text — quiet luxury, no warm fill.
options.case: Strongest fix if the complaint is “beige buttons”; consciously leaves golden brass behind.
options.risk: Less Mediterranean warmth; CTAs compete with body ink unless weight/size stay clear.

options.label: Olive Atelier
options.thesis: Deep olive leaf as action — botanical Marbella without terracotta-on-cream cliché.
options.viewport: Deep olive primary fill with parchment label; parchment grounds unchanged.
options.case: Fresh accent that still feels Costa del Sol landscape, not tech-purple or hotel gold.
options.risk: Shifts brand metaphor from metal hardware to garden/landscape.

options.label: Costa Slate
options.thesis: Cool Mediterranean slate-teal — architectural water and stone, not brass hardware.
options.viewport: Slate-teal primary on parchment and dark bands; parchment/near-white label.
options.case: Cooler luxury for interior architecture; clear break from beige-brass.
options.risk: Cooler temperature vs warm parchment — must stay deep enough to avoid spa-teal.

options.label: Oxidized Copper
options.thesis: Warm oxidized copper — FF&E metal honesty, richer and redder than beige brass.
options.viewport: Copper-red primary fill with parchment label; still One Accent Rule.
options.case: Keeps material/metal story but escapes the gold-beige reading.
options.risk: Near terracotta family — must stay dark and rare so it doesn’t flip into AI cream+clay.
